title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1971-04-26
lineage: SBD > MR > Shure line mixers > Sony R2R (7.5 ips) > BASF 90m > Revox B77 > Alesis Masterlink ML9600 > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording of the April 26 1971 Fillmore East show delivers a high‑energy performance with Duane Allman’s legendary solos on It Hurts Me Too and Hard to Handle, captured in good but not flawless sound quality.
ai_review.review: The show is praised for its fiery second‑set jams – especially the dueling guitar work on It Hurts Me Too and a scorching Hard to Handle – as well as strong first‑set moments like Dark Star → Wharf Rat. The soundboard source is generally clear, though listeners note a long tuning intro on Sugar Magnolia, a cut‑off of I Know You Rider, and occasional song‑order quirks.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4–5 stars, highlighting standout performances and decent sound quality; only a few technical complaints lower the average slightly.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp start and clear instrument separation, but includes lengthy tuning on Sugar Magnolia, a truncated I Know You Rider track, and minor song‑order issues; overall listenable.

poor_songs: Sugar Magnolia (considered okay but not earth‑shaking)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong first set with a classic Dark Star and tight jams, followed by a second set highlighted by Duane Allman’s guest solos and an energetic Good Lovin jam; overall pacing keeps the momentum high.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Mentioned as laying back while dueling with Duane; not blown off stage but his interplay is noted.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for earth‑shaking bass bombs and powerful stomping during jams.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drums segment leading into Good Lovin praised for its funky, twisty jam.
